Justin Miller, Development Planner, attended the meeting to present an overview of the application, highlight key points from the Planning Report, and respond to questions from the Committee.
Discussion
Wolman Navarro Torres, 400 Albert Street, Woodstock, the Owner and Applicant, attended the meeting to express support for the report and respond to questions from Committee members.

No further questions were asked, and no one voiced opposition to the application.
Moved by
Peter Rigby
Seconded by

That the City of Woodstock Committee of Adjustment
approve
Application MV27-26, submitted by Wolman Navarro Torres for lands described as Part of Lot 21, 26 Plan 77 Parts 1 and 2 41R- 10455; T/W 401795; S/T easement over Part 2 41R-10455 as in WK48002, being municipally known as 400 Albert Street, in the City of Woodstock, as it relates to:
Section 5.2.8 Additional Residential Units, Table 3A – Regulations for Additional Residential Units (ARUs); to increase the Maximum Permitted Size for additional residential units from 100 m2 (1,076.4 ft2) to 117 m2 (1,259.4 ft2) to permit two additional residential units in an existing dwelling, subject to the following condition:
I. If approved, a building permit is required to create the additional residential units.
The proposed relief meets the
four tests
of a minor variance as set out in Section 45(1) of the Planning Act as follows:
The proposed relief represents a minor variance from the provisions of the City’s Zoning By-law in that the increased additional residential unit size will remain clearly secondary to the principal dwelling unit and is desirable for the development of the lands.
The proposed relief maintains the general intent and purpose of the City’s Zoning By-law, and no negative impacts are anticipated associated with the proposed size of the additional residential units.
The relief sought is desirable for the use of the land as it will allow for development permitted by the Zoning By-law.
The relief maintains the intent and purpose of the Official Plan as the proposed relief will facilitate development contemplated within the Low Density designation.
And further that any comments received from the public were reviewed and considered before the decision was made in relation to this planning matter.
Carried
